findings.description: The 'data' bucket sets no ACL restriction and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, and the inline comment confirms it is intended to be public; the customer master spreadsheet uploaded to it would therefore be readable by anonymous principals.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects (including customer-master.xlsx) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
No logging block is configured on a bucket that is publicly reachable and holds customer data, so unauthorized reads leave no audit trail for detection or forensics.
No bucket policy denying requests with aws:SecureTransport=false is attached, so objects in this publicly readable bucket can be retrieved over cleartext HTTP.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data in public unencrypted bucket
findings.description: customer-master.xlsx, a customer master data file, is uploaded to the public, unencrypted aws_s3_bucket.data with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id set, directly exposing PII and storing it unencrypted.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial records are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for this bucket holding financial data, eliminating the audit trail needed to detect unauthorized access.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could expose financial data publicly with no account-level guardrail.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for the operations bucket, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to this bucket is not auditable.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for this bucket, so nothing prevents a later public ACL or policy from exposing its contents.
The data_science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so analytics datasets are stored unencrypted at rest, unlike the logs bucket which uses SSE-KMS.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public ACLs or policies on this bucket.

The log bucket uses the 'log-delivery-write' canned ACL, which grants write/read-ACP to the LogDelivery group, and has no public access block preventing a future public or cross-account grant on audit log data.
